Bot.description: Bot as returned by the `GET /bots` method of its channel API. Only the common fields are listed; other fields depend on the channel. When empty, it is returned as an empty array `[]` instead of an object `{}`

channel_data.description: Channel-specific bot data. When empty, it is returned as an empty array `[]` instead of an object `{}`

id.description: Bot ID; ObjectId or UUID depending on the channel

inbox.description: Number of received and unread messages

settings.description: Channel-specific bot settings. When empty, it is returned as an empty array `[]` instead of an object `{}`

statistics.description: Channel-specific bot statistics. When empty, it is returned as an empty array `[]` instead of an object `{}`

status.description:
* `1` - new

                    * `2` - reconnect required

                    * `3` - active

                    * `4` - deleted

                    * `5` - inactive

                    * `8` - ready to be deleted

                    * `10` - activation in progress

                    * `11` - action required

                    * `12` - deactivated

is_trashed.description: Whether the dialog is deleted; always `false` in the list

label_ids.description: IDs of labels assigned to the dialog

field.description: Field name to filter by (e.g., label_ids)

info.description:
Using the API for Chatbots, you can integrate your system with SendPulse’s chatbots service and get detailed information about your account, bots, dialogs.

            
On the right, there is a button for authorizing requests made on this page. Click “Authorize,” then insert the ID and Secret from your account.

            
To perform a request directly from the page, click the "Try it out" button within each method block. Then fill in input fields if any (for URL parameters, the description is right below the URL request; for body parameters, the description is under the “Scheme” button to the right of the example), and click “Run.” You'll find the server response and description of received parameters below.
info.title: Chatbots service API

get.description: Returns information about your current account pricing plan, the number of messages in your plan, bots, contacts, list of tags, and variables
get.x-ai-description: This endpoint returns a consolidated snapshot of the current SendPulse account: active pricing plan, remaining message/email quotas, number of chatbots, contacts, and the full set of tags and variables. It is the primary diagnostic entry point — use it to understand account limits and available resources before planning campaigns, imports, or automations that may hit plan constraints.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Call this endpoint early when the user asks about limits, quotas, remaining messages, or plan tier, instead of guessing capacity.
Before initiating bulk operations (mass mailings, large imports), check the remaining message count and plan limits to avoid quota overruns.
Use the returned tags and variables lists to validate names the user references, preventing calls with non-existent tags/variables.
Treat this as a read-only operation — it never modifies account state, so it is safe to call for refreshing context.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Lead with the current pricing plan and the most relevant quota (e.g., remaining emails/messages) to the user's question.
Present contact and bot counts as plain numbers; avoid dumping the full raw payload unless asked.
If quotas are low or near the limit, proactively warn the user and suggest upgrading the plan or reducing send volume.
When the user asked about a specific tag or variable, confirm whether it exists in the returned lists.
x-ai-suggestions: Review your remaining message quota before scheduling a mass campaign.
Use `getMailingLists` to inspect contacts within specific address books.
If limits are reached, consider upgrading your pricing plan.

200.description: Bots of all channels of the account. Bots of channels whose service did not respond are omitted. Note: Bridge bots are currently returned as one nested array element instead of separate items

get.summary: Get a list of connected bots
get.x-ai-description: This endpoint provides a unified inventory of all chatbots connected across every messaging channel (Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Viber, Live Chat, and others) in the account. It is the primary discovery operation for chatbot orchestration: before interacting with flows, subscribers, or messages, an agent must first resolve the target bot's ID and channel from this list. Unread message counters surface bots that need operator attention, while bot status reveals which channels are active versus disconnected. Channels whose upstream service is temporarily unavailable are silently omitted, so an absent bot does not necessarily mean it was deleted.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Call this endpoint first whenever a task references a bot by name or channel rather than by ID, to resolve the correct bot ID.
If an expected bot is missing from the response, do not assume it was deleted — its channel's service may have failed to respond; suggest retrying before concluding the bot is gone.
Use the unread message counts to prioritize which bots require immediate operator or automation attention.
Check each bot's status before attempting write operations; skip or warn about bots that are inactive or disconnected.
Be aware that Bridge bots are currently returned as a single nested array element rather than as separate items, and account for this when counting or iterating bots.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Group bots by channel so the user can quickly see coverage across Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram, and other platforms.
Highlight bots with unread messages, stating the count, so the user knows where attention is needed.
Flag any bot whose status is not active, and mention that channels with an unresponsive service may be missing from the list.
When referencing a specific bot for a follow-up action, surface its bot ID explicitly so it can be reused.
x-ai-suggestions: Use the returned bot ID with the bot-specific endpoints to fetch flows, subscribers, or messages.
If a bot shows unread messages, retrieve its recent conversations to respond to subscribers.
If an expected channel's bot is missing, retry the request since its service may have been temporarily unavailable.

get.description: Returns the list of all dialog labels created on the account
get.summary: Get all dialog labels for account
get.x-ai-description: This endpoint retrieves the full catalog of dialog labels configured on the account. Labels are the organizational taxonomy used to classify, segment, and route conversations in SendPulse chatbots and live-chat. Fetch them first to obtain valid label IDs before assigning labels to dialogs, filtering conversations, or building automation rules — they act as the source of truth for any label-driven workflow.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Call this endpoint before any operation that assigns, filters, or removes a label, so you can resolve human-readable label names to their IDs.
Cache the returned list within the session to avoid redundant calls, but refresh it if a label was just created or deleted.
If the account has no labels yet, treat an empty list as a valid state and suggest creating a label rather than reporting an error.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Present labels in a readable form, pairing each name with its ID so the user can reference them unambiguously.
If the list is empty, inform the user that no dialog labels exist yet and offer to create one.
When the user intends to tag a conversation, map their requested label name to the matching ID from this response.
x-ai-suggestions: Use the returned label IDs with the dialog-tagging endpoint to classify a conversation.
If the needed label is missing, create it before proceeding.
Filter the dialogs list by a label ID to review all conversations under a given category.

post.description: Creates a new dialog label with emoji and name

400.description: Label limit reached (maximum 16 labels per account)

422.description: Validation failed, e.g., missing required fields or invalid emoji

post.x-ai-description: Creates a dialog label — a visual tag (emoji + name) used to categorize and triage chatbot conversations. Labels are a finite, account-scoped resource capped at 16 entries, so each one should represent a meaningful, reusable workflow category (e.g., 'needs follow-up', 'VIP', 'resolved') rather than an ad-hoc marker. Reaching the limit blocks creation until an existing label is removed.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Before creating, fetch existing labels to confirm the account is below the 16-label limit and that no semantically duplicate label already exists.
Validate that the emoji is a single valid Unicode emoji and the name is concise and descriptive to avoid a 422 response.
If the limit (16) is already reached, do not call this endpoint; instead advise deleting or reusing an existing label.
Prefer broad, reusable category names over one-off labels to conserve the limited label slots.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Confirm success by stating the new label's ID, name, and emoji.
On a 400 response, explain that the 16-label account limit has been reached and suggest deleting an unused label before retrying.
On a 422 response, point to the specific invalid field (missing name or invalid emoji) and show a corrected example.
Suggest assigning the new label to relevant dialogs as the next step.
x-ai-suggestions: needs_follow_up
vip_customer
resolved
awaiting_payment

post.description: Replace the set of labels assigned to a dialog. An empty array removes all labels.

label_ids.description: Array of label IDs to assign to the dialog

200.description: Whether the labels of the dialog were updated

422.description: Validation failed: invalid or unknown dialog ID, invalid label IDs or label does not exist

post.x-ai-description: This endpoint performs a full replacement of the label set on a dialog, not an incremental add. Labels in SendPulse chatbots are the primary mechanism for segmenting, routing, and triaging conversations (e.g. 'VIP', 'Needs human', 'Spam'). Because the operation is idempotent and overwrites the entire set, the caller must send the complete desired list every time — any previously assigned label omitted from the array will be removed. Sending an empty array is the canonical way to clear all labels from a dialog.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: This is a REPLACE operation, not an append. Before calling, fetch the dialog's current labels and merge them with the new ones if the user intends to ADD labels rather than overwrite the set.
Resolve human-readable label names to their IDs first; this endpoint accepts only label IDs, not names.
Validate that every label ID in `label_ids` actually exists before calling — an unknown or invalid ID triggers a 422 validation error.
Respect the hard limit of 16 labels per dialog (`maxItems`); do not attempt to exceed it.
Ensure `label_ids` contains no duplicates, as the field requires unique items.
If the user's goal is to remove all labels, send an empty `label_ids` array intentionally rather than skipping the field.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Confirm the outcome by stating which labels are now assigned to the dialog after the replacement.
If labels were removed as a side effect of the overwrite, explicitly call that out so the user is not surprised.
On a successful empty-array call, confirm that all labels were cleared from the dialog.
On a 422 error, explain whether the problem was an unknown dialog ID or an invalid/non-existent label ID, and suggest verifying the IDs.
On a 403, clarify that the account lacks permission to manage labels on this dialog.
x-ai-suggestions: List available dialog labels with `getDialogLabels` to resolve names to IDs before assigning.
Retrieve the dialog's current labels before overwriting to preserve existing ones when the intent is to add.
After updating labels, filter or route dialogs by the new label set.

delete.description: Deletes a label. The label is also removed from all dialogs where it was assigned.
delete.x-ai-description: This endpoint permanently removes a dialog label from the account and detaches it from every dialog it was assigned to. In SendPulse chatbot/live-chat workflows, dialog labels are classification markers used for routing, filtering, and reporting on conversations. Deletion is a cascading operation: it does not merely delete the label definition but also strips it from all historical and active dialogs, which can affect saved filters, analytics segments, and automation rules that depend on this label.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Verify the label exists by its ID before attempting deletion to avoid a 404 and to confirm you are targeting the correct label.
Warn the user that this action is irreversible and that the label will be removed from all dialogs where it was assigned, not just unlinked from a single conversation.
Check whether the label is referenced by any active filters, segments, or automations, since deletion may break them.
If the user intends to rename or reorganize rather than remove, suggest editing the label instead of deleting it.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Confirm the deletion by referencing the deleted label ID and stating that it was also removed from all associated dialogs.
If the response indicates the label was not found (404), explain that the label may have already been deleted or the ID is incorrect, and suggest listing existing labels to verify.
Remind the user that any filters or reports relying on this label will no longer return it.
If the operation failed due to permissions (403), explain that the current account role lacks rights to manage dialog labels.

put.description: Updates emoji and name of an existing dialog label

422.description: Validation failed, e.g., invalid emoji or name

confirmation.description: Overwrites the emoji and name of an existing dialog label, affecting all dialogs currently tagged with it.

put.x-ai-description: Updates the emoji and display name of an existing dialog label. Dialog labels are organizational markers used to categorize and triage conversations (dialogs) in chat and messaging workflows. Editing a label propagates the new emoji/name to every dialog already tagged with it, so this is a non-destructive metadata change that affects the visual taxonomy across the whole inbox — not the label-to-dialog assignments themselves.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Confirm the target dialog_label ID exists before updating; if the agent is unsure, list existing labels first to resolve the correct ID instead of guessing.
Send only the fields that need to change, but respect that the endpoint expects the full DialogLabelInput payload — preserve the current emoji or name when the user wants to change only one of them.
Validate the emoji is a single valid emoji character and the name is non-empty and within allowed length before calling, to avoid a 422 Validation failed response.
Treat 404 as a signal that the label ID is stale or wrong, not that the operation failed logically — re-resolve the ID.
Because renaming affects every dialog tagged with this label, flag potentially disruptive changes (e.g. repurposing a widely used label) before proceeding.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Confirm the update by stating the label's new emoji and name together with its ID.
If the change renamed a label in active use, note that all dialogs tagged with it now reflect the new label.
On 422, explain which input failed validation (invalid emoji or name) and show a corrected example.
On 404, tell the user the label was not found and offer to list current labels so they can pick the right one.
On 401/403, clarify that the token is missing, invalid, or lacks permission to manage dialog labels.
x-ai-suggestions: List all dialog labels with `getDialogLabels` to confirm the current emoji/name before editing.
Apply the updated label to conversations using the dialog assignment endpoints.
Remove the label entirely with `deleteDialogLabel` if it is no longer needed.

get.description: Returns information about your dialogs from all channels

parameters.description: The ID of the last_inbox_message element after which elements will be returned
parameters.name: search_after

get.x-ai-description: This endpoint retrieves a paginated, cross-channel inventory of conversations (dialogs) from all connected messengers and chat sources (Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Live Chat, Viber, etc.). A 'dialog' is the aggregation unit of customer communication — it groups messages with a single contact into one conversational thread. Use it as the entry point for triaging the inbox, locating active conversations, or building an omnichannel support overview before drilling into a specific dialog's messages.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: This is a read-only listing operation — it never mutates state, so it is safe to call for discovery and triage without confirmation.

Use `size` and `skip` for basic pagination, but prefer cursor-based pagination via `search_after` for deep or stable traversal of large inboxes, since offset pagination can drift as new dialogs arrive.
To paginate with `search_after`, pass the ID of the `last_inbox_message` from the last element of the previous page; do not combine it blindly with large `skip` values.
Respect the `search_after` constraints (string, 1–32 chars); an out-of-range or malformed value will trigger a 422 response.
Use `order` to control sorting (e.g., by most recent activity) when the user wants the newest or oldest conversations first.
If a 401 or 403 is returned, verify the access token and that the account has chatbot/inbox permissions before retrying.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Summarize the dialogs concisely: channel, contact, and last message context rather than dumping raw payloads.
Indicate whether more pages are available and explain how to fetch them (via `search_after` cursor or increased `skip`).
When presenting many dialogs, group or highlight by channel so the user can quickly see where activity is concentrated.
If the list is empty, clarify that no dialogs match the current filters rather than implying an error.
On a 422, explain which pagination parameter was invalid (commonly `search_after`) and how to correct it.
x-ai-suggestions: Retrieve messages of a specific dialog using its ID to read the full conversation thread.
Fetch the next page by passing the last element's `last_inbox_message` ID into `search_after`.
Filter or sort results with the `order` parameter to surface the most recent conversations first.

post.description: Returns dialogs filtered by specified criteria. Supports filtering by label_ids and other fields.
post.x-ai-description: This endpoint retrieves dialogs (conversation threads) that match a structured filter. In SendPulse chatbots, a 'dialog' represents an ongoing conversation with a subscriber across a messaging channel. The filter uses a recursive boolean expression tree (type: and/or) combining field operators (e.g. 'in', 'eq') on fields like label_ids, enabling precise segmentation of conversations by tags, status, or other attributes. Use it to triage, route, or analyze support workloads rather than scanning all dialogs manually.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Resolve human-readable labels to their label_ids (ObjectId format) before building the filter — users refer to labels by name, not ID.
Compose the filter as a nested boolean tree: wrap conditions in a top-level 'and'/'or' expression and place field operators (operator, field, value) as leaf expressions.
Use the 'in' operator with an array value when matching against multiple label_ids; prefer 'eq' for single-value exact matches.
If no filter is provided, expect the endpoint to return all dialogs (paged) — warn the user this may be large and suggest narrowing by labels or status.
Account for pagination: the response is a page object, so plan to iterate if the full result set is needed.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Report the number of dialogs found and note whether results are paginated (more pages may exist).
Summarize dialogs by the criteria that matched (e.g. which labels), not just raw IDs, so the user understands the segment.
If zero dialogs match, suggest relaxing the filter or verifying that the label_ids are correct.
On a 422 error, explain which filter field or operator was invalid and propose a corrected expression structure.
Suggest a logical next action such as assigning, replying to, or labeling the returned dialogs.
x-ai-suggestions: Retrieve full conversation history for a returned dialog using the dialog's ID.
Apply or remove labels in bulk on the matched dialogs.
Combine label filters with status conditions (open/closed) to build a support triage queue.

get.x-ai-description: This endpoint retrieves all operator groups configured on the account. Operator groups are organizational units that bundle live-chat operators together for routing incoming conversations, distributing workload, and managing team-based permissions. Use it as the discovery step before assigning operators, routing chats to a specific team, or auditing how support staff are structured.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Call this endpoint first when the user needs to reference a group by ID (e.g., for routing or assignment), since group IDs are not known in advance.
If the account has many groups, rely on pagination metadata in the response rather than assuming a single page contains all groups.
Match groups by name case-insensitively when the user refers to a team by name, as names may vary in capitalization.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Present the groups as a concise list showing each group's name and ID; mention the owner's user ID only if the user asks about ownership.
If no groups exist, explain that operator groups must be created before operators can be organized into teams.
When the user intends a follow-up action, surface the relevant group ID so it can be reused in the next call.
x-ai-suggestions: Use a returned group ID to assign operators or route incoming chats to that team.
If the needed group is missing, create a new operator group before proceeding.
Review group membership to balance workload across support teams.
